## 1 Scope

This part of [IEC 61784-2 def] issues extensions of [Communication Profile] () and for Real-Time Network Components (RTE) [RFC 819](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3795.txt#page20) applies a Real-Time Network (RTE) communication profile (CP) and related network components based on the IEC 61158 series (Type 27), ISO/IEC/IEEE 8802-3 and other standards.

For each RTE communication profile, this document also specifies the relevant RTE performance indicators and the dependencies between these RTE performance indicators.

**NOTE 1. All CPs are based on standards or draft standards or International Standards published by the IEC or on standards or International Standards established by other standards bodies or open standards processes.**

**NOTE 2. The RTE communication profile uses ISO/IEC/IEEE 8802-3 communication networks and its related network components and in some cases amend those standards to obtain RTE features.**

**NOTE 3. Some CPs of [RFC 19](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3673.txt#page20) are specified in IEC 61784-1-19.**

## 2 Normative references

The following documents are referred to in the text in such a way that some or all of their content constitutes requirements of this document. For dated references, only the edition cited applies. For undated references, the latest edition of the referenced document (including any amendments) applies.

# 3.4 Glossary

- **Information element (n)**: The smallest transferable unit in the UPC/DT of information.
- **Information transfer activity (acc)**: The superset of the actual information transfer (urn).
- **Desirable (DS)**: Maintaining or committing an information transfer action.
- **Requirement (Q)**: Structure for directing the reconfiguration of information transfer resources to the task flow transferable (Flow) are defined in Federation (Foreign) Unit Node (Rule).
- **It is important to note that the flow is described in a lower case letter.** It is important to note that the flow is described in a lower case letter.

# 3.5 Other Terms

\begin{itemize}
  \item TP (Transfer Bit) – A point in the transfer bit pattern of the information transfer context.
  \item Consumable domains – Usually addresses [...]\newline
  \item ID – It is not necessarily fixed, it is generated by the distributed network management processing. It may change as the network environment changes, dynamic changes, nodes fail, lost internet connection... and other uncertain events occur. \newline
  \item GC (Gate Command) – It is a part of initiating a PUF to generate a weak key that can be further used to initialize the mutual authentication. It is usually used as the first part of the key exchange process on the network.
\end{itemize}

### 4 CPF 19 (MECHATROLINK¹) – RTE communication profiles

#### 4.1 General overview

Communication Profile Family 19 defines communication profiles (CPs) based on IEC 61158-2 type 24, IEC 61158-3-24, IEC 61158-4-24, IEC 61158-5-24 and IEC 61158-6-24, and on IEC 61158-2 type 27, IEC 61158-5-27, and IEC 61158-6-27, and on other standards (see Table 2 and Table 3).

The CPF 19 (MECHATROLINK) consists of four distinct protocol sets, known generically (for historical reasons) as MECHATROLINK-II (M-II) for CP 19/1, MECHATROLINK-III (M-III) for CP 19/2, Σ-LINK II for CP19/3, and MECHATROLINK-4 (M-4) for CP 19/4, which have major differences in their physical layers.

- MECHATROLINK-II (Profile 19/1, M-II): based on TIA-485-A PhL, which operates at 10 Mbit/s, and provides for additional features (IEC 61784-1-19, 4.2);

---

Compliance with this profile does not require use of the trade names. Use of the trade name MECHATROLINK requires permission of the trade name holder.

### Data Link

The Physical Layer of the CP 19/4 shall be according to ISO/IEC/IEEE 8802-3. The bit rate shall be 100 Mbit/s or 1 000 Mbit/s. But mixing both 100 Mbit/s and 1 000 Mbit/s is not allowed in the same network.

### Data Link layer

The Data Link Layer shall be according to ISO/IEC/IEEE 8802-3.

### Application Layer

The Application layer specified in IEC 61158-5-27 and IEC 61158-6-27 shall be used.

### M-4 Master

The application layer is described in IEC 61158-5-27 and IEC 61158-6-27. Table 4 specifies the use of the services specified in IEC 61158-5-27, included in this profile.

### Page 25

dash line.### 4.2.4.2.2 Delivery time

The $DT$(Delivery time) for CP19/4 is shown in Formula (1).

$$DT = T_{synchWidth} + T_{domainAllWidth} + T_{ipWith} + T_{ctrlWidth} + T_{guardWidth}$$

(1)

where

$DT$ is the delivery time;
$T_{synchWidth}$ is the synchronization band;
$T_{domainAllWidth}$ is the I/O data exchange band;
$T_{ipWidth}$ is the IP communication band for Internet Protocols (Option). It shall be set by application;
$T_{ctrlWidth}$ is the network control band (Option);
$T_{guardWidth}$ is the guard time.

The $T_{synchWidth}$ is shown in Formula (2).

$$T_{synchWidth} = T_{tr}(L_{sync}) + \max_{n_{all} \in N_{all}} \left\{ T_{cable}(n_{sm}, n_{all}) + \sum_{n_{r} \in N_{r}(n_{sm}, n_{all})} T_{relay}(n_{r}) \right\} + T_{fig}$$

(2)

where

$T_{tr}(L)$ is the packet propagation time (packet length is $L$ bytes);
$L_{sync}$ is the length of synchronization packet;
$N_{all}$ is all stations on the network;
$n_{all}$ is the element of $N_{all}$;
$T_{cable}(n_{s}, n_{d})$ is the cable delay time from station $n_{s}$ to station $n_{d}$;
$n_{sm}$ is the synchronization master;
$N_{r}(n_{s}, n_{d})$ is the delay time of repeat (depends on implementation);
$n_{r}$ is the number of hops between master and slave;
$T_{relay}(n)$ is the delay time for relay of station $n$;
$T_{fig}$ is the inter frame-packet gap.

The $T_{domainAllWidth}$ is shown in Formula (3).

$$T_{domainAllWidth} = \max_{d \in D} \{ T_{domainStart}(d) + T_{domainWidth}(d) \} + T_{domainAllStart}$$

(3)

where

$D$ is the collection of control domain;
$d$ is the element of control domain $D$;
$T_{domainStart}(d)$ is the transmission start time of control domain $d$;
$T_{domainWidth}(d)$ is the transmission width of control domain $d$.

The $T_{ctrlWidth}$ is shown in Formula (4).

The slave station is triggered to generate an event when it receives a synchronization notification frame that is periodically sent from the synchronization master station. With this, synchronization accuracy of periodic events in the cyclic communication state is guaranteed.

Void.
